name: Anwar Ibrahim
role: Prime Minister, Malaysia; on the Balabac EDCA base and Sabah defense, August 19, 2026
quote: As a neighbouring country closely affected by claims over Sabah, we are somewhat concerned with the tension... at the very least, our basic defence capabilities must be strengthened.

name: Ferdinand Marcos Jr.
role: President, Philippines; confirming the 'provisional understanding' on Sierra Madre resupply and China oil-and-gas talks, August 14, 2026
quote: We have to find new ways... this discussion has gained prominence. And where we are now, I think we have moved forward.

name: Rear Admiral Roy Vincent Trinidad
role: AFP Spokesperson for the West Philippine Sea; on Ayungin Shoal and BRP Sierra Madre, August 11, 2026
quote: BRP Sierra Madre nor Second Thomas Shoal or Ayungin Shoal will never be abandoned. We need not seek approval, nor inform any foreign power in performing our mandate.

name: Xi Jinping
role: General Secretary, Communist Party of China; President, PRC
quote: As a coastal state in the South China Sea, China firmly upholds its territorial sovereignty and maritime rights and interests in accordance with its domestic law and international law.

name: Wang Yi
role: Director, Office of the Central Foreign Affairs Commission; Foreign Minister, PRC
quote: Infringement and provocation in the South China Sea will backfire and those acting as others' chess pieces are bound to be discarded.

name: Sun Weidong
role: Vice Foreign Minister, PRC; Led China delegation at 11th BCM / 24th FMC Talks, Quanzhou (March 27–28, 2026)
quote: China calls on the Philippines to take concrete actions to translate goodwill into real results on South China Sea maritime cooperation and energy development.

name: Mao Ning
role: Spokesperson, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, PRC
quote: Japan and the Philippines' launch of so-called 'maritime boundary delimitation talks' is completely illegal and invalid, seriously infringing upon China's maritime rights and interests. China has taken necessary actions in response and urges both sides to immediately cease all illegal actions.

name: Zhao Lijian
role: Former Spokesperson, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, PRC
quote: AUKUS seriously undermines regional peace and stability, intensifies the arms race and undermines the international non-proliferation regime. China firmly opposes it.

name: Ferdinand Marcos Jr.
role: President of the Philippines (since June 2022)
quote: The Philippines cannot yield. The Philippines cannot waver. The West Philippine Sea is ours and will remain ours.

name: Gilberto Teodoro
role: Secretary of National Defense, Philippines
quote: We have no choice but really to be resilient and to stand up against Chinese aggression. Manila remains under severe threat from China territorially and politically — and that will not change because of diplomatic summitry elsewhere.

name: Enrique Manalo
role: Secretary of Foreign Affairs, Philippines (2022–2025)
quote: It's clear that many of China's recent incidents are inconsistent with its declared intention to manage differences. We have no intention of surrendering or compromising sovereign rights.

name: Ma. Theresa P. Lazaro
role: Secretary of Foreign Affairs, Philippines; Chair, 59th ASEAN AMM (May 7, 2026)
quote: Completing the South China Sea Code of Conduct is something we owe the world. The Philippines will not yield on our sovereign rights, and we will continue to pursue every diplomatic avenue to uphold international law and UNCLOS.

name: Jay Tarriela
role: PCG Rear Admiral; West Philippine Sea spokesperson
quote: The use of cyanide by Chinese fishing vessels near the BRP Sierra Madre is not just environmental sabotage — it is an act designed to starve our marines and weaken our presence at Ayungin Shoal. We will document every tactic China employs against our garrison.

name: Romeo Brawner Jr.
role: Chief of Staff, Armed Forces of the Philippines (2023–2024)
quote: What happened on June 17 was an aggressive and illegal use of force against our personnel. Our men showed extraordinary restraint and courage under direct physical assault.

name: Rodrigo Duterte
role: Former President of the Philippines (2016–2022)
quote: The Americans are the ones pushing the Philippine government to go out there and find a quarrel and eventually maybe start a war.

name: Joe Biden
role: President of the United States (2021–2025)
quote: Any attack on Philippine aircraft, vessels, or Armed Forces in the South China Sea would invoke our mutual defense treaty. That commitment is ironclad.

name: Pete Hegseth
role: Secretary of Defense, United States; Shangri-La Dialogue keynote speaker, May 31, 2026
quote: We are entering a new era of pragmatic idealism in the Indo-Pacific. The US-China strategic stability agreement is meaningful for the history of peace in this region — but it does not diminish our commitment to allies, or our position that any unilateral attempt to change the South China Sea status quo by force or coercion is unacceptable.

name: Lloyd Austin
role: Secretary of Defense, United States (2021–2025)
quote: The US commitment to the Philippines' defense is ironclad. We are establishing Task Force Ayungin to ensure we can decisively respond to crisis or aggression in the South China Sea.

name: Antony Blinken
role: Secretary of State, United States (2021–2025)
quote: The Philippines is an irreplaceable ally. Armed attacks on Philippine armed forces, public vessels, or aircraft in the Pacific, including the South China Sea, invoke our mutual defense obligations.

name: Samuel Paparo
role: Commander, US Indo-Pacific Command (since 2024)
quote: The death of a Filipino citizen in the South China Sea would represent a red line, as stated by President Marcos. We stand ready to fulfill our treaty obligations without hesitation.

name: Anthony Albanese
role: Prime Minister of Australia (since May 2022)
quote: AUKUS has one overriding objective: to enhance the stability of the Indo-Pacific. This is the biggest single investment in Australia's defence capability in all of our history.

name: Lee Hsien Loong
role: Prime Minister of Singapore (2004–2024); Senior Statesman
quote: ASEAN countries do not want to be forced to choose between the US and China. We need to see both powers manage their relationship and coexist peacefully.

name: Fumio Kishida
role: Prime Minister of Japan (2021–2024)
quote: Ukraine today may be East Asia tomorrow. Japan must take robust action to deter any attempt to change the status quo by force in the Indo-Pacific.

name: Shigeru Ishiba
role: Prime Minister of Japan (since October 2024)
quote: The creation of an Asian version of NATO is essential to deter China. We must synthesize QUAD, AUKUS, and bilateral alliances into a collective Asia security architecture.

name: Rishi Sunak
role: Prime Minister of the United Kingdom (2022–2024)
quote: AUKUS represents a new era of cooperation between our three nations. Together we are investing in the security and stability of the Indo-Pacific for generations to come.

name: Catherine Vautrin
role: Minister of the Armed Forces, France
quote: The SOVFA with the Philippines reflects France's commitment to a free and open Indo-Pacific. We are not bystanders — France has sovereign territory and strategic interests in the Pacific, and we stand with partners who uphold international law.

name: Romeo Brawner Jr.
role: Chief of Staff, Armed Forces of the Philippines (2024–present)
quote: Balikatan 2026 will be the biggest in history. Japan will send combat-capable units for the first time since World War II. This is what a free and open Indo-Pacific looks like — and China is watching.

name: Anwar Ibrahim
role: Prime Minister of Malaysia; 2026 ASEAN Chair
quote: Malaysia will urge ASEAN and China to fast-track negotiations on a binding Code of Conduct for the South China Sea. 2026 is the year we must get this done — for regional stability and for the rule of law.

name: Shinjiro Koizumi
role: Minister of Defense, Japan (since November 2024)
quote: Japan's participation in Balikatan 2026 demonstrates our commitment to a free and open Indo-Pacific and the interoperability of our alliance with the Philippines. Japan's Self-Defense Forces stand with our partners to uphold regional stability and international law.

name: Guo Jiakun
role: Spokesperson, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, PRC (current)
quote: Those who play with fire will get burned. Pulling in extra-regional countries to flex muscles, engage in targeted confrontation, and ratchet up tensions does not serve regional peace and stability.

name: Ronnie Gil Gavan
role: Commandant, Philippine Coast Guard; Ordered deployment of BRP Cape San Agustin vs. CCG 4305 off Zambales (May 2026)
quote: We will never allow the normalization of illegal patrols in Philippine EEZ waters. Every unauthorized Chinese vessel in our waters will be confronted, documented, and challenged — that is not optional, it is our duty under Philippine law and international law.

name: Arvin Lagamon
role: Deputy Chief of Staff, Armed Forces of the Philippines; Key voice on WPS cognitive and information warfare
quote: We are already at war. Not yet a kinetic war, but the political war, the economic war, and more importantly, the cyber and informational war are already going on. We confront daily illegal, coercive, aggressive, deceptive, destructive, and bullying activities in the West Philippine Sea.

name: Roy Trinidad
role: Rear Admiral, PCG; West Philippine Sea Spokesperson
quote: The modern battlefield is the mindset of the Filipino people. We need to protect the cognitive domain of the Filipino people — China's information operations are designed to normalize its illegal presence and undermine Philippine public resolve in the West Philippine Sea.

name: Antonio T. Carpio
role: Former Associate Justice, Supreme Court of the Philippines (2001–2019); Senior SCS Legal Authority
quote: China's 'marine nature reserve' claim at Scarborough Shoal follows the same playbook used at Fiery Cross Reef and Subi Reef — civilian installations that become military bases. If China constructs permanent infrastructure at Scarborough under the guise of conservation, it will be irreversible. The Philippines must challenge this at every stage.

name: Lawrence Wong
role: Prime Minister of Singapore (since May 2024); Attended 48th ASEAN Summit, Cebu, May 7-8, 2026
quote: ASEAN must chart its own course — not be defined by the competition of major powers. The ASEAN Maritime Centre and the Coast Guard Forum are practical steps to manage SCS tensions without being drawn into great-power rivalry.

name: Malcolm Turnbull
role: Former Prime Minister of Australia (2015–2018); AUKUS critic; Chatham House address, May 2026
quote: AUKUS is a huge wealth transfer from the Australian government to the US and the UK. Australia will not receive nuclear submarines for many years while paying tens of billions for the privilege — and the promise of Australian-built submarines remains deeply uncertain.

name: Richard Marles
role: Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Defence, Australia; AUKUS Defence Ministerial, Shangri-La Dialogue, May 30, 2026
quote: AUKUS Pillar II delivers its first signature project — uncrewed undersea vehicles that will enhance allied maritime superiority across the Indo-Pacific. Australia's commitment to AUKUS and the submarine pathway is steadfast: this is about peace, stability, and deterrence in our region.

name: John Healey
role: Secretary of State for Defence, United Kingdom; AUKUS Defence Ministerial, Shangri-La Dialogue, May 30, 2026
quote: The AUKUS UUV signature project demonstrates that Pillar II delivers real capability — early, tangible, and trilateral. The UK remains committed to AUKUS, to the submarine pathway, and to a free and open Indo-Pacific.

name: Gilberto Teodoro Jr.
role: Secretary of National Defense, Philippines; 10th Anniversary of SCS Arbitral Award, July 12, 2026
quote: We should implement it ourselves; that is the strategy. The nine-dash line is false.

name: Ma. Theresa Lazaro
role: Secretary of Foreign Affairs, Philippines; South China Sea Code of Conduct talks, June 10, 2026
quote: Negotiations are no longer quarterly — they are now monthly. We are pushing to conclude the Code of Conduct by the end of 2026.

name: Mao Ning
role: Spokesperson, Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs; on Japan-Philippines EEZ talks, May 29, 2026
quote: The so-called delimitation negotiations between Japan and the Philippines are entirely illegal and invalid.
